title: Define policy schema + validation for SLO-based auto-rollback thresholds
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
We need a first-class config schema for auto-rollback policies driven by latency/error SLO monitors.

This ticket defines:
- Canonical policy schema (how customers/config authors express thresholds) scoped by route/model/region/customer tier.
- Migration path from existing rollout policy config (which today only captures traffic split strategy + manual gates).
- Server-side validation rules to prevent unsafe or noisy rollbacks (low-traffic, bad windows, missing scope selectors, etc.).

This is the schema consumed by the Rollout Controller evaluator/executor and surfaced in Console (read-only display initially, then editable by authorized operators).

Non-goal: implement the evaluator logic itself (ENG-2314) or monitor identity contract (ADR-0147) beyond ensuring the schema aligns with it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A versioned schema exists for SLO rollback policy config that supports:
  - scopes by route_id, model_id, region, and customer_tier (with explicit precedence rules)
  - separate latency and error policies (independently enable/disable)
  - evaluation windows and min traffic guardrails
  - cooldown and max rollbacks per period
  - optional baseline comparison semantics (must be worse than prior stable)
- Policy can be stored/retrieved via control-plane config persistence (backed by existing rollout policy storage) without breaking existing rollouts.
- Validation rejects invalid/unsafe configs with actionable error messages (returned to Console/API).
- Migration plan documented and implemented behind a feature flag so we can roll out safely.
- Unit tests cover precedence resolution and validation for at least 10 representative configs (good + bad).
implementation_notes:
Proposed schema (v1) to live under rollout policy, keyed by rollout target (route/model pair) with optional overrides.

Terminology:
- "scope": selector determining where a policy applies (route/model required at some level; region/tier optional).
- "effective policy": the resolved policy after applying precedence.

Schema outline (conceptual; exact wire format determined in PR):
- policy_version: "v1"
- enabled: true|false
- default_policy:
  - latency:
    - enabled
    - objective: p95_ms | p99_ms (choose one for v1; default p95)
    - threshold_ms
    - window: 5m|10m|15m (enumerated)
    - min_requests: integer
    - warmup_grace: 2m|5m (do not evaluate immediately after step change)
    - must_be_worse_than_baseline: true|false
  - error:
    - enabled
    - metric: 5xx_rate | request_error_rate
    - threshold_rate (0..1)
    - window: 5m|10m|15m
    - min_requests
    - warmup_grace
    - must_be_worse_than_baseline
  - rollback:
    - cooldown: 10m|20m|30m
    - max_rollbacks_per_6h: integer (default 2)
    - fail_behavior_on_monitor_unavailable: fail_open|fail_closed|unknown (v1 recommendation: unknown -> no rollback)
- overrides: list of scoped overrides with selector + partial policy patch.

Precedence (highest to lowest):
1) exact match: route+model+region+tier
2) route+model+region
3) route+model+tier
4) route+model
5) route only (optional; only if we decide to support route-wide defaults)
6) global default (for internal canaries only; NOT for external tenants by default)

Note: For v1, we should require at least route+model at default_policy level for external tenants to avoid accidental global enablement. Internal canary may allow global defaults behind a flag.

Storage:
- Store as JSON blob in rollout_policy_config with explicit version field.
- Add server-side canonicalization: sort overrides deterministically, fill defaults, strip unknown fields (or reject unknown fields; prefer reject for safety).

Console display:
- Provide an "Effective policy" view per rollout target in ENG-2316; this ticket only ensures schema supports deterministic resolution and has clear serialization.
migration_plan:
Current state:
- rollout policies exist for traffic shifting/canary but have no SLO rollback config.

Migration approach:
1) Add new nullable field auto_rollback_policy to rollout policy record. Existing records remain valid.
2) Gate evaluation on BOTH:
   - feature flag: auto_rollback.slo_policy_enabled
   - presence of a valid policy blob (policy_version=v1)
3) Migration script/backfill:
   - No automatic enablement for customer tenants.
   - For internal canary routes, optionally backfill a conservative default policy (requires explicit approval from SRE + PM).
4) Forward compatibility:
   - Require policy_version in stored blob.
   - Reject unknown policy_version with error "unsupported policy version".
5) Rollback plan:
   - If issues observed, disable feature flag; schema remains stored but unused.

Open question captured below: whether we should support a "shadow" mode where evaluator computes verdict without executing rollback. If yes, include top-level mode: shadow|enforced (default shadow for internal).
validation_rules:
Validation must run on write (Console/API) and on read (defensive; if legacy data exists).

Hard validation failures (reject):
- Missing policy_version.
- window not in allowed set.
- threshold_ms <= 0.
- threshold_rate <= 0 or > 1.
- min_requests < 0.
- cooldown not in allowed set OR cooldown < window (to avoid immediate re-triggering).
- max_rollbacks_per_6h < 1.
- overrides selector missing required identifiers OR selector is ambiguous (e.g., tier provided without route+model).
- both latency.enabled=false and error.enabled=false while enabled=true (policy enabled but no signals).

Soft validation (warn/normalize; stored with canonical defaults):
- min_requests=0 -> set to default (latency: 200 req/window; error: 500 req/window) unless explicitly allowed for internal.
- warmup_grace omitted -> default 5m for external tenants, 2m for internal.
- must_be_worse_than_baseline omitted -> default true (per SRE guidance) when baseline exists.

Safety constraints:
- Enforce an upper bound on scope fanout for a single write (e.g., limit overrides list length to 100) to avoid huge configs.
- Ensure policy does not permit global enablement for external tenants unless tenant is allowlisted (flag + allowlist).

Error messages:
- Must include JSON pointer-like path to the offending field (e.g., "overrides[3].latency.threshold_ms") and a short remediation hint.
open_questions:
- Should v1 support burn-rate semantics directly, or keep evaluator logic separate and accept only fixed thresholds? (Tentative: schema supports fixed thresholds only; burn-rate can be v2 if we decide.)
- Do we need separate thresholds per deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), or do tier+region cover enough? (PM feedback suggests tier+region is sufficient for v1; Dedicated may need tighter latency later.)
- Do we want a first-class "mode": shadow vs enforced? (SRE prefers shadow for internal ramp; PM prefers it as an internal-only switch.)
- Should we allow route-only policies (no model) to simplify ops, or does that risk accidental broad enablement? (Leaning no for external tenants.)

comments: 2025-02-06 (Jordan Lee): Creating this ticket to unblock ENG-2314. Need schema locked early to avoid rework across control-plane + console.
2025-02-08 (Michael Nguyen): Drafted v1 schema proposal + precedence rules. Next: validate with Paula/Marissa on scoping needs and with Miles/Sean on guardrails (min traffic + cooldown).

2025-02-10 (Paula Mendes): Please ensure per-region overrides are supported and that we can express different defaults for enterprise tiers (Dedicated) vs self-serve. Also want policy to be visible in Console even if not editable yet.

2025-02-11 (Sean Gallagher): Strong preference: must_be_worse_than_baseline default true; require warmup_grace to avoid canary ramp noise. Also do NOT rollback on monitor outage; unknown verdict should block rollback but still notify.

2025-02-13 (Michael Nguyen): Updated validation: cooldown >= window enforced; added max_rollbacks_per_6h. Added tenant allowlist requirement to prevent global enablement. Pushed draft PR for review (will link once up).

2025-02-17 (Jordan Lee): Reviewed schema diff — looks good. Remaining concern: whether to allow route-only policies; I’m aligned with keeping route+model required for external tenants. Please add explicit error message for ambiguous selectors.
2025-02-18 (Michael Nguyen): Marking In Review. Added unit tests for precedence resolution and a table-driven validation suite. Waiting on final sign-off from SRE on default min_requests values.
